questions.rationale: The objective is a single parentage fact for the subject, and the tree holds no parent links for him. The three sibling persons (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) have no parent links either, so they cannot yet be used to infer parents. The 1930 residences place the family in Nueva Italia, which bounds where to look.

Searched without a hit: Parácuaro civil births 1908-1912 (indexed), Parácuaro baptisms (indexed and full-text sampling), El Caulote fallback, the parents' marriage in Michoacán and in Guerrero, and La Unión baptism for Miguel. Leads found but not read, and unsearched pages of the Parácuaro baptism volumes, are listed as deferred. Skipped by the researcher: the 1999 death record, siblings' later records, and the full-text backup search.

items.rationale: Tree records Liborio Cruz born 23 Jul 1916 at Pochutla and Facundo Cruz born 27 Nov 1918 at Rosario, both Coahuayutla, Guerrero, and neither has parent links. Their baptisms name both parents, the most direct route to the parents of the family (siblings are the objective's chosen route; sibling status of Mauro is itself unproven until parents match). loc_002: civil registers for Coahuayutla start only 1921, so San Agustín parish is the primary source; Libro 15 (Oct 1910-Aug 1917) and Libro 2 (Apr 1915-Jan 1919) are covered by Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records (name-searchable); baptisms from May 1912 are out of order, so browse images if search fails. Search surname Cruz alone (Hispanic indexing quirk), variants Cruz/Corona, and also look for a Mauro baptism (circa 1910) in the same volumes.

items.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico
items.rationale: Tree records Miguel Cruz born 24 Apr 1913 at El Coco, La Unión; no parents linked. Search the San Felipe de Jesús parish baptism and the civil birth (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration; both collections name-searchable) for 1913 to get parents' names to compare with the Coahuayutla couple. loc_003: Guerrero civil records were archived at district (Montes de Oca) level, parish volumes only partly name-indexed, so browse the 1913 volume; also check Petatlán, which took part of La Unión's territory in 1867.

Tree places Mauro, Miguel, Liborio and Facundo in Nueva Italia in 1930. The Mexico National Census, 1930 (name-searchable) is filed under Parácuaro municipality (loc_001), not Nueva Italia. Read the household in full: parents if co-resident, relationships, ages and birthplaces, which tests whether the four are brothers and gives parent names to match against the baptisms. Verify against the image, and neighbors on the page are FAN leads (compadres, relatives).

Mauro's own civil birth entry would name both parents. Nueva Italia founded 1909 and sat in Parácuaro municipality (loc_001), so search Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration (collection 1916243), Parácuaro nacimientos 1910-1912 (the catalog lists those years; 1913-1915 and 1918 are missing). Birth is only 'about 1910', so widen to 1908-1912 and try Cruz and Corona variants; registration was irregular, so absence is weak evidence.

Mauro's baptism in Parácuaro parish (baptisms 1838-1958 per loc_001, held by the Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán; Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, collection 1883388) would name parents and godparents (FAN). Window runs to 1915 because baptism could follow birth by years and the civil register has gaps in 1913-1915.

Fallback if Parácuaro parish and civil registers do not hold Mauro: loc_001 names neighboring El Caulote parish (Archivo Diocesano de Tácambaro, registers 1882-1971) as the next place to check, and 'near Nueva Italia' leaves the birth parish uncertain. Also consider Apatzingán.

Dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage to each other in Michoacán (civil matrimonios 1881-1931 and parish marriages 1864-1942, plus información matrimonial 1853-1967), once names come from items 1-3. It would confirm the couple as a unit, supply the mother's name (the surname Corona comes only from Mauro's own name and is not treated as her proven maiden name; no remarriage is known), and its date relative to about 1910 corroborates but does not by itself prove Mauro is their child. Window is the parents' likely marriage years before the first known birth.

Parallel marriage search in Guerrero, since the family was in La Unión by 1913 and Coahuayutla by 1916 and the parents may have married in either (San Felipe de Jesús, San Agustín parishes; civil registers under Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration). Same purpose as the Michoacán marriage item; search by father's name and Cruz plus Corona once parents are named. Marriage investigation files may state parents' origins.

Tree records Mauro's death 21 Apr 1999 at Nueva Italia. Baptism may not be reachable (birthplace uncertain, 1913-1915 civil gap), so his own death certificate, which usually names parents, is planned. Filed after 1942 under Múgica municipality (loc_001), at the Registro Civil of Múgica or Michoacán state archive; the FamilySearch Michoacán civil collection ends 1940, so likely needs a request by the researcher or descendants rather than an online search.

## Conclusion

The evidence indicates that Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 to 1912 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, was the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (probable). His mother is possibly **Apolinar Corona** (possible, not yet at the level of a likely finding). The two parents are tiered separately because the father is named in the groom's own marriage entry with a clean identity link, while the mother's name on that entry carries an unexplained element. The stored overall tier is the stronger of the two.

## Direct evidence

The only record in which Mauro himself names his parents is his Catholic marriage entry at Parácuaro, Michoacán, 20-21 February 1941. Mauro Cruz, groom, aged 29, is recorded as the child of Sostenes Cruz and "Ma Apolinar Corona"; the bride was Esperanza Ramirez. Mauro was the informant, which is firsthand knowledge, but a parent's name given at one's own wedding is secondary information as to parentage, and the entry is a derivative index ("México, Michoacán, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1555-1996", FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-89NS, Entry for Mauro Cruz and Sostenes Cruz, 20 de febrero de 1941). The image (ark:/61903/3:1:939L-9NX2-R) was not viewed. Age 29 gives birth in 1911-1912, one to two years after the tree's "about 1910"; this is compatible and does not bear on identity.

## Corroborating evidence

Two Guerrero baptisms from San Agustín, Coahuayutla record brothers born to the same couple: Liborio Cruz Corona, christened 27 August 1916, child of Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona ("México, Guerrero, registros parroquiales, 1576-1979", FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6C1W-839Q, Entry for Liborio Cruz Corona and Sóstenes Cruz, 27 Aug 1916); and Facundo Cruz "Crona", christened 13 December 1918, child of Sóstenes Cruz and Apolina Crona (same collection, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6C1S-H8QF, Entry for Facundo Cruz Corona and Sóstenes Cruz, 13 Dec 1918). Both are derivative indexes with the presenting parent as informant, so they are one family-informant evidence unit, not two independent ones. They show a couple with the parent names Mauro gave in 1941 and the double-surname form Cruz Corona that Mauro's tree name carries. The 1930 census of Nueva Italia de Ruiz lists Apolinar Corona, widowed, born about 1880-81 in Guerrero, in a household with Primitivo, Mauro, Migel, Libario and Facundo Cruz, all born in Guerrero ("México censo nacional, 1930", FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZC2, Entry for Feliciano Anguiano and Senaida Ferrel, 1930). The census records no relationships and its informant is unknown; it places the woman and the brothers in Mauro's home locality, consistent with Sóstenes being dead or absent by 1930.

## Weaknesses and how they were weighed

- **The mother's name on the 1941 entry.** It reads "Ma Apolinar Corona"; no other record has the "Ma" element. Person-evidence links that mother persona to Apolinar Corona only at speculative, so the maternity claim is held at possible until the element is explained (for example by Mauro's 1936 marriage entry or a baptism entry for him). Surname, given name and role otherwise match and nothing contradicts.
- **Census Mauro not linked.** The 1930 census Mauro is recorded as born in Guerrero, while the tree has Michoacán. That persona was not linked and nothing here relies on it. The marriage record gives no birthplace, so this is not a conflict between the cited sources; a Guerrero birth would fit the family's 1916-1918 residence in Coahuayutla. A birth or baptism record for Mauro would settle it.
- **No independent original.** All sources are derivative; the parents' own marriage and Mauro's birth or baptism record were not found.
- No conflicts are registered for this question.

## Tier

Probable for paternity, possible for maternity; overall bookkeeping tier probable. Proved is not reached for either: there is no original birth or baptism entry for Mauro, no independent primary source, and the search was not reasonably exhaustive.

## What could advance it

Mauro's baptism in the unread Parácuaro baptism volumes (1913-1917, and the unsampled pages of 1906-1913 and 1918-1921), his 1936 Nueva Italia church marriage, the images of the 1941 and baptism records, and his 1999 civil death record.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia (Parácuaro municipality through 1941; Múgica municipality from 1942), Michoacán, Mexico (1880-1940)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Nueva Italia:** founded 1909 (FamilySearch standard place "Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico", dateRange +1909/) as a hacienda/company-town colony in the Tierra Caliente region of western Michoacán.
- **Governing municipality for the 1880-1940 target period:** Parácuaro, Michoacan, Mexico (municipality formed 1861; FamilySearch standardPlace dateRange +1861/). The municipality of Múgica, which today contains Nueva Italia, was not created until 1942 (standardPlace dateRange +1942/) — two years after the end of the target window.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** state of Michoacán, Mexico.
- **Diocese:** Catholic parish records for Parácuaro are held by the Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (per FamilySearch Catalog koha:162793).
- **Economy/period note:** no population-figure data was returned for Parácuaro by this survey's place_population call (error: no data found for this standardPlace); no claim about population size is made here.
- Wikipedia confirms Nueva Italia is a city in the Tierra Caliente Michoacana region of Michoacán (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nueva_Italia%2C_Michoac%C3%A1n), but gives no further detail usable for records research.

## Boundary changes
- Nueva Italia itself did not exist as a place before 1909; for any event before that date, search only under the parent municipality, Parácuaro.
- From 1880 through 1941 (which covers the entire 1880-1940 target period), Nueva Italia's civil-registration and parish records were created and filed under the municipality of Parácuaro, Michoacán.
- The municipality of Múgica was carved out in 1942, after the end of the target period — records for Mauro Cruz Corona's circa-1910 birth will not be found under "Múgica" as a jurisdiction; they are filed under "Parácuaro."
- This is a continuous research trail, not two unrelated record sets: search "Parácuaro, Michoacán" for 1880-1940 events, and only switch to "Múgica, Michoacán" for events after 1942.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** municipality-level civil registration (Registro Civil) began nationwide in Mexico on 28 July 1859 by presidential decree, but was not vigorously enforced until the republic was restored in 1867 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration). For Michoacán specifically, the FamilySearch collection "Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration" covers 1859-1940 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
- **What exists for Parácuaro:** FamilySearch Catalog entry koha:200572, "Registros civiles del municipio de Parácuaro, 1881-1931" (births/nacimientos 1881-1930, marriages/matrimonios 1881-1931, deaths/defunciones 1881-1931), microfilmed from the Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán, viewable online via collection 1916243. `volume_search` independently confirms 100%-indexed Matrimonios volumes for Parácuaro for 1901, 1903, 1905, 1907, 1908, 1909, 1910, 1912, 1919, 1920, among 159 "Vital" volumes total for 1880-1940 (48 Birth, 58 Death, 53 Marriage).
- **Where held:** originals at the Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán; FamilySearch holds microfilm copies (images 4871472-4871488) and offers an online index-and-image collection.
- **Gaps:** nacimientos (births) are missing for 1913-1915 and 1918 per the catalog's film list (which jumps 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922); defunciones missing 1913-1915; matrimonios run largely continuous but a 1913-1916 gap appears there too — consistent with disruption during the Mexican Revolution.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish baptismal, marriage, and burial registers (below) — the civil registration page explicitly recommends using both together, since compliance was imperfect (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration).

### Church records
- **Denomination present:** Roman Catholic (the dominant religion in Mexico for centuries, per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Getting_Started).
- **Record types for Parácuaro parish:** FamilySearch Catalog koha:162793, "Registros parroquiales, 1838-1967" — bautismos (baptisms) 1838-1958, confirmaciones (confirmations) 1884-1959, matrimonios (marriages) 1864-1942, información matrimonial (marriage investigation files) 1853-1967, and entierros (burials) 1838-1887 only (no later burial volumes listed in the catalog entry).
- **Where held:** originals at the parish archive and the Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán; FamilySearch microfilm images 4036756-4737557, also reachable via "Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records" (collection 1883388).
- **Gaps:** no burial (entierros) register beyond 1887 is listed in the catalog for Parácuaro — for a death after 1887, rely on the civil defunciones series above rather than church burial records.
- **Language:** Spanish; read with the Spanish Genealogical Word List (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List) and BYU's Spanish paleography tutorial.
- Note: a neighboring parish, El Caulote (anciently "Furicato"), also in this area, is separately catalogued (koha:309382) under the Archivo Diocesano de Tácambaro with its own baptism/marriage/death registers 1882-1971 — worth checking if Parácuaro's own registers do not yield the family.

### Census records
- **National census:** the 1930 Mexico National Census is indexed and imaged online at FamilySearch (collection 1307314) and Ancestry (collection 1771); a FamilySearch Catalog entry (koha:668871) separately confirms a 1930 "Censo de población del municipio de Parácuaro, Michoacán" microfilm (image group 4107250), held at the Archivo General de la Nación.
- **Other enumerations:** `volume_search`'s summary counts 2 "Census" volumes for Parácuaro within 1880-1940 — consistent only with the 1930 census; no earlier Michoacán state/municipal census was found in this survey for this place.
- **Access:** the 1930 national census is name-indexed with images online; earlier censuses (if any survive) were not located and would require direct inquiry to the Archivo General de la Nación.

### Probate and court records
- No Parácuaro-specific probate, will, or court records surfaced in collections_search, volume_search, or catalog_search for this survey — this is a coverage gap, not evidence such records never existed.
- Civil-law Mexico uses testamentos (wills) and notarial records for estate matters, typically filed with a local notary (notario público) or municipal court; none specific to Parácuaro were found online or in the Catalog in this survey.

### Land records
- **Survey/distribution system:** not addressed by any page or tool result returned in this survey — no `{Jurisdiction}_Land_and_Property` page exists for Parácuaro or Michoacán in the corpus reachable here, so this guide cannot state the land-distribution office. Treat as unconfirmed.
- Nueva Italia was an early-20th-century hacienda colonization project; land records, if they survive, would most likely be with state or federal land offices, but no tool result in this survey names the specific office.

### Military records
- No Michoacán- or Parácuaro-specific military, pension, or draft record collection surfaced in this survey's collections_search, volume_search, or catalog_search results.
- The Mexican Revolution (roughly 1910-1920) directly overlaps the target period and likely explains the registration gaps noted above (civil nacimientos/defunciones missing 1913-1915); no revolution-specific service or casualty record set for this place was found here.

### Cemetery records
- No Parácuaro- or Nueva Italia-specific cemetery index or sexton register was returned by any tool in this survey. Not addressed by external_links_search results for this place either.

### Newspaper records
- No Parácuaro- or Nueva Italia-specific newspaper collection or archive was returned in this survey. "El Informador: Diario Independiente, 1917-present" (http://hemeroteca.informador.com.mx/) was returned as a general Mexico-wide newspaper resource by external_links_search, but it is a Guadalajara (Jalisco) paper, not local to Michoacán.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not a border or port locality, but Mexican emigration to the United States was common from this period — relevant record sets returned by external_links_search include: "Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895-1964" (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) and "US Border Crossings from Mexico to United States" (FamilySearch collection 1803932, per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Border_Crossings_from_Mexico_to_United_States_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
- These cover the subject's likely emigration if the family later moved to the US; they do not cover events that stayed in Mexico.

### Tax records
- No Parácuaro-specific tax record collection or catalog entry was returned in this survey.

### Other record types
- None identified for this place beyond those listed above in this survey's results.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940 (collection 1916243); Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records (collection 1883388); Mexico National Census, 1930 (collection 1307314); Parácuaro civil/church microfilm images (4871472-4871488, 4036756-4737557) | Primary births/marriages/deaths and baptisms/marriages/burials for Parácuaro | Free |
| Ancestry | 1930 Mexico National Census (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1771); México, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1567-1970 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60038/); Mexico Select Baptisms/Deaths/Marriages indexes (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9297, /9298, /9299); Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895-1964 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) | Alternate index for the same civil/church record types, plus US-bound border crossings | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Mexico Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths indexes (http://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30039/, -30040/, -30041/) | Alternate index for births/marriages/deaths NOT online elsewhere as images | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` for Parácuaro 1880-1940 matched 201 digitized volumes total; only the first 10 (all 1901-1920 Matrimonios) were detailed above — the remaining volumes (births, deaths, and other marriage years) were not individually examined in this survey.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán | Original civil registration (births, marriages, deaths) for Parácuaro municipality | In-person or written request to the state archive |
| Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán | Original Catholic parish registers for Parácuaro (baptisms, confirmations, marriages, marriage investigations, burials to 1887) | In-person or written request |
| Archivo Diocesano de Tácambaro | Original Catholic parish registers for the neighboring El Caulote parish | In-person or written request |
| Archivo General de la Nación | 1930 municipal census microfilm for Parácuaro | In-person or written request; also reachable via FamilySearch microfilm |

## Records NOT online
- Parácuaro's probate/will/notarial records, land records, military/pension records, cemetery records, newspaper archives, and tax records were not found in any online database by this survey (see the "Not addressed" notes in each subsection above) — their absence from search results is a digitization gap, not evidence they don't exist.
- Many Parácuaro civil-registration and church-register images on FamilySearch are browsable by microfilm image group even where a name index is incomplete; always check both search and browse.

## Known record losses
- No tool result in this survey states that any Parácuaro record series was destroyed. The apparent gaps in civil nacimientos/defunciones around 1913-1916 (during the Mexican Revolution) are inferred from missing years in the Catalog's film list, not a documented loss — no source confirms destruction versus non-filming versus the records simply not surviving.
- The 1930 census and the online civil/church collections are confirmed survivors and the primary substitute where a given year is missing from another series.

## Research tips
- Search both civil registration (Registro Civil, 1859 on) and the parallel Catholic parish registers for the same event — compliance with civil registration was inconsistent until 1867, so church records may exist where civil ones don't, and vice versa for 20th-century events (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration).
- Always search for an ancestor's siblings' birth records first — they corroborate or extend what's known about the parents (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- Find the parents' marriage record: it typically gives information leading to their own birth records, then repeat the process up each generation (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- When searching FamilySearch's index, try only the paternal (first) surname — most indexed Hispanic-naming records were indexed with one surname only, even though two are customary (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org).
- If Mauro Cruz Corona is not found under Parácuaro, search the neighboring parish of El Caulote (Archivo Diocesano de Tácambaro) and consider browsing by image where the index may be incomplete.
- For 1910-1920, expect gaps and irregular filing due to the Mexican Revolution; broaden date ranges when searching birth/death indexes for that span.

- **Municipal seat:** Coahuayutla de Guerrero (also the parish seat, San Agustín parish).
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Costa Grande region, Guerrero, Mexico; Guerrero became a Mexican state on October 27, 1849 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Guerrero,_Mexico_Genealogy).
- **Population:** approximately 13,000 as of the Wikipedia figure cited on the locality page (no period-specific 1880-1940 figure was returned by place_population, which found no data for this place).
- **Localities within the municipality:** Barrio de Lozano, Coahuayutla de Guerrero, Galeana de abajo, Los Balsas, Matamoros, Nueva Cuadrilla, Zacatula (per the same locality page). Pochutla and Rosario are not among these named places; treat them as smaller ranchos likely recorded under the cabecera parish/civil registers until confirmed otherwise.
- **Religious denomination:** Catholic — the municipality was served by the parish of San Agustín, Coahuayutla, under the Archivo Diocesano de Chilapa (FamilySearch Catalog koha:1037615).
- **Key historical context relevant to records:** the family's 1916-1918 residency falls in the Mexican Revolution period, which commonly disrupted civil registration continuity in rural Guerrero — consistent with the large gaps seen in the catalogued civil-registration microfilm for this municipality (see Vital records below).

## Boundary changes
- No boundary change specific to Coahuayutla was returned by any tool during this survey; the municipality's existence since 1868 is treated as stable through 1880-1940.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Mexican civil registration began nationally in 1859 but was not strictly enforced until 1867 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Guerrero,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records); held at the municipality level. For Coahuayutla specifically, the earliest catalogued civil-registration microfilm (koha:819525) is "Registros civiles del municipio de Coahuayutla, 1921-1973" — i.e. the municipal civil registers actually surveyed on film start in 1921, after the family's 1916-1918 Pochutla/Rosario period.
- **What exists:** births, marriages, deaths for the municipality, 1921-1973 on film (filmNumber 1950734: Nacimientos 1921, 1924, 1926-1927, "años faltan meses" [some months missing]; 1950735: Nacimientos 1928-1929, 1932; Matrimonios 1921, 1924, 1926-1928, 1932, 1940, 1962, 1966, 1973). Online, these fall within collection 1918291, "Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860-1996" (8,406,460 persons, state-wide).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch online (collection 1918291) and FamilySearch Library/Granite Mountain Vault microfilm (koha:819525); originals at the Archivo Estatal del Registro Civil del estado de Guerrero.
- **Gaps:** no civil register for Coahuayutla was found on film or online for 1916-1918 — the family's known Pochutla/Rosario years — and even the earliest surveyed years (1921+) have missing months. For this period, Catholic parish registers are the primary substitute (see Church records).

### Church records
- **Denomination present:** Catholic, parish of San Agustín, Coahuayutla (Archivo Diocesano de Chilapa), covering 1819-1930 per catalog entry koha:1037615.
- **Record types:** baptisms, confirmations, marriages, marriage informations (información matrimonial), deaths.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch online as part of collection 1823323, "Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576-1979" (21,256,652 persons, state-wide); microfilm at FamilySearch Library (filmNumbers 1506782-1506787). Specific volumes covering the family's window: baptisms Oct 1910-Aug 1917 (Libro 15, image group 004600366_005_M94D-DT2, 98% indexed) and Apr 1915-Jan 1919 (Libro 2, image group 004600366_007_M94D-DTG, 95% indexed); marriage/death and información matrimonial volumes spanning 1910-1921 are also catalogued (filmNumber 1506787).
- **Gaps:** baptisms "mayo 1912-1932 (en disorden)" are noted as out of chronological order on the microfilm (koha:1037615) — expect to browse rather than rely on strict date filing; no gap for 1916-1918 itself was identified.
- **Language:** Spanish.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** Mexico National Census, 1930 (collection 1307314), outside the 1916-1918 window but useful to retrospectively confirm family composition and birthplaces.
- **Municipal census:** "Censo de población del municipio de Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1930" (catalog koha:421889, filmNumber 1507392), also outside the target window.
- **Other enumerations:** `volume_search` summary counted 4 Census-group volumes for this place/period overall; none specific to 1916-1918 were returned.
- **Access:** the 1930 national census is online and indexed at FamilySearch (collection 1307314); the 1930 municipal census is on microfilm, viewable online per the catalog note.

### Probate and court records
- No Coahuayutla-specific probate/court collection was returned by `collections_search`, `volume_search`, or `catalog_search` in this survey. Treat this as a coverage gap — physical probate records, if they survive, would be held by the Guerrero state archives or local courthouse; this was not confirmed by any tool.

### Land records
- No Coahuayutla-specific land-record collection was returned by this survey. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that none exist; consult the Guerrero state archives (see Repository guide).

### Military records
- The family's 1916-1918 period falls within the Mexican Revolution; no Coahuayutla-specific military/service record collection was returned by this survey. None confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki or catalog for this place.

### Cemetery records
- The locality page for Coahuayutla explicitly states "None found" for cemeteries. FindAGrave and BillionGraves indexes exist for Guerrero generally (per the state Genealogy page), but no Coahuayutla-specific cemetery data was returned.

### Newspaper records
- No Coahuayutla- or Guerrero-specific newspaper archive was returned by this survey beyond the general Mexico-wide "Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México" and "El Informador" links surfaced by `external_links_search` (national/regional, not Coahuayutla-specific).

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not a border or port locality; no port-of-entry records apply. If descendants later emigrated, Ancestry's "Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895-1964" (collection 1082, per external_links_search) would be the relevant collection, but this is background, not local-period material.

### Tax records
- No Coahuayutla-specific tax-record collection was returned by this survey.

### Other record types

# Locality Guide: El Coco, La Unión, Guerrero, Mexico (1880-1940)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, admitted with Guerrero statehood October 27, 1849; the town of La Unión was made the municipal seat in 1870, and by 1884 the surrounding area was organized as the "Montes de Oca" judicial district (FamilySearch place records show a "Montes de Oca, Guerrero" Judicial District dated +1898/+1985).
- **County/municipal seat:** La Unión (town).
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Guerrero, Mexico (capital Chilpancingo de los Bravo); region "Costa Grande."
- **Population:** State-level only is available — Guerrero state populstat estimates: ~353,200 (1882), ~479,200 (1900), ~594,300 (1910), ~641,700 (1930), ~732,900 (1940). No per-municipality population figure for La Unión was returned by place_population; the municipality's Wikipedia-sourced figure on its FamilySearch Wiki page (~26,000) is a modern count, not period data.
- **Economy/geography:** Coastal Pacific municipality within the Costa Grande region of Guerrero, bordering the state of Michoacán.
- **Religious denominations:** Catholic (parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión, is the confirmed local parish).
- **Key historical events:** The municipality ceded territory in 1867 to create Petatlán (later reinstated to La Unión); the Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) fell within the target period and disrupted both civil and church recordkeeping nationally.

## Boundary changes
- 1849: Guerrero became a state, separate from México state.
- 1867 (Feb 14): La Unión ceded part of its territory to create the municipality of Petatlán; that area was later reinstated to La Unión (FamilySearch Wiki, La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca Genealogy page).
- 1870: the town of La Unión was made the municipal seat.
- By 1884: the area was organized under the "Montes de Oca" district name for civil-registration archiving purposes — this is an administrative (district) layer above the municipality, not a boundary change to the municipality itself.
- No further boundary changes in the 1880–1940 window were found in the tools used.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Mexico's civil registration law dates to 1859 (President Juárez, Veracruz); enforcement nationwide was weak until 1867. Guerrero civil records are recorded at the municipio level but archived at the district level (FamilySearch Wiki, Mexico Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration) — here, the Montes de Oca district.
- **What exists:** FamilySearch collection "Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860-1996" (collection id 1918291; 8,406,460 person entries statewide) covers births, marriages, deaths with index & images, subject to contractual visibility limits. The FamilySearch Catalog also holds "Registros civiles del distrito de Montes de Oca, 1898-1985" (catalog id koha:664584, images) specific to this district.
- **Where held:** Civil registry state archives for Guerrero per the FamilySearch Wiki collection page; images/index at FamilySearch (collection 1918291); Ancestry.com also lists separate Guerrero civil registration Births (1860-1947), Marriages (1863-1954), and Deaths (1860-1987) index-and-image collections (subscription).
- **Gaps:** Pre-1867 coverage is weak nationally due to non-enforcement; this makes the 1878-on parish baptism registers (below) the stronger source for the early part of the target window.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión (baptisms from 1878).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Catholic (Diocese: Archivo Diocesano de Chilapa, per FamilySearch Catalog entry koha:1037663).
- **Record types:** Baptisms, confirmations, and marriages, from the parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión, Guerrero, 1878-1931 (catalog id koha:1037663; microfilms 1506788 and 1506789).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog/Granite Mountain Record Vault microfilm, online via "Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576-1979" (collection id 1823323, 21,256,652 person entries statewide). volume_search confirms digitized baptism volumes for San Felipe de Jesús spanning 1878-1889, 1890-1931 in multiple volumes, confirmations 1902-1930, and marriages 1878-1930.
- **Access detail:** Of 41 volumes matched for this place/period, baptism volumes range 77-96% name-indexed and full-text searchable; one confirmations volume (imageGroupNumber 004605080_028_M946-7D2, 1902-1909) is 0% name-indexed though full-text searchable; one 1929-1931 baptism volume (imageGroupNumber 004605080_015_M946-7D4) shows 0 images and is not full-text searchable — effectively unusable as currently cataloged and worth flagging for FamilySearch follow-up.
- **Gaps:** The catalog note states "Bautismos 1878-1931 (faltan años)" — years are missing within that span; exact missing years are not specified.
- **Language:** Spanish.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** "Mexico National Census, 1930" is online at FamilySearch (collection 1307314), and the FamilySearch Catalog holds "Censo de población del municipio de La Unión, Guerrero, 1930" specifically (catalog id koha:424445; microfilms 1507425, 1507436 covering Leg. 1-6). volume_search's summary counts 7 Census-group volumes for this place/period (none yet browse-only or full-text-only flagged in that count, i.e. status not further broken out there).
- **State/provincial census:** None found in tools used for this period.
- **Access:** The 1930 census is described by the FamilySearch Wiki civil-registration page as useful to cross-check whether a family married civilly, by the Church, or both.

### Probate and court records
- No Guerrero- or La Unión-specific probate/court collection was returned by collections_search, volume_search, or catalog_search in this survey. This is a coverage gap in the tools used, not evidence such records do not exist — probate matters in Mexico of this era were typically handled by municipal/district courts (juzgados) and would be held physically, not digitized.
- **Where held:** Not identified by any tool in this survey; likely the district court archive (Montes de Oca district) or state judicial archives — unconfirmed.

### Land records

- Not confirmed by any tool result in this survey; treat as a gap.
